description: Provenance-backed real-code Security mini-suite. Each vulnerable case cites a real CVE/GHSA advisory or a documented public teaching write-up with a real commit, license, and URL — not an invented label on an arbitrary OSS file. Scope: single-file Security review only (no cross-file Architecture claims scored here).

cases.why_visible_single_file: StaticResource._handle skips the filepath.relative_to(self._directory) containment check entirely when follow_symlinks=True, before calling .resolve(). No other file/route participates in the check.
cases.adaptation_note: Verbatim class/method excerpt from the tagged source; unrelated methods trimmed for brevity.

cases.why_visible_single_file: Repo._clone passes a caller-controlled url and multi_options straight into the git.clone(...) subprocess call with no protocol allowlist or unsafe-flag denylist. The disclosed PoCs (ext:: URL, --upload-pack= injection) exploit only this function.
cases.adaptation_note: Repo._clone body is a close excerpt of git/repo/base.py; a minimal Git stub class was added so the file parses standalone without the full GitPython package installed.

cases.advisory: Documented teaching write-up (CWE-639), not a CVE
cases.why_visible_single_file: note_detail is @login_required but the lookup get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk) is scoped to the whole table, not request.user. Any authenticated caller reads any note by pk. The fixed twin in the same commit adds owner=request.user.
cases.adaptation_note: Docstring/decorator/lookup line verbatim from upstream; inline HTML strings re-wrapped because the fetch used to pull the file stripped angle brackets (logic unchanged).

cases.fix_reference: >=1.8.2 removed the hardcoded key (per advisory); exact diff not verified against upstream for this suite
cases.why_visible_single_file: Django SECRET_KEY signs session cookies; a literal value here lets anyone reading the source forge a valid session (advisory's own repro uses salted_hmac with the leaked key). No other file is needed.
cases.adaptation_note: SECRET_KEY literal and the SECURITY WARNING comment above it are quoted verbatim from the advisory's reproduction steps. Surrounding settings lines are minimal reconstructed boilerplate (NOT a copy of upstream settings.py, which is a large multi-purpose file not verified verbatim). The clean counterpart is a representative env-var control, not an upstream file.
